subject: science
skillName: Matter Is Made of Tiny Particles

items.prompt:
What is all matter made of?
A) Tiny particles too small to see
B) Only solid blocks
C) Nothing at all
D) Only water
items.answer: A) Tiny particles too small to see

steps: All matter is built from extremely small particles.

items.prompt:
In which state are particles spread the farthest apart?
A) Solid
B) Liquid
C) Gas
D) They are always the same

steps: Gas particles move freely and are spaced far apart.

items.prompt:
You can smell food cooking from another room because
A) sound carries the smell
B) tiny particles spread through the air to your nose
C) the food grows larger
D) light carries the smell
items.answer: B) tiny particles spread through the air to your nose

steps: Particles leave the food and travel through the air.

items.prompt:
A balloon weighs more after it is filled with air. This is evidence that
A) air is not matter
B) air has no particles
C) air is matter and has weight
D) the balloon shrank
items.answer: C) air is matter and has weight

steps: The added air particles add mass, so the balloon weighs more.

items.prompt:
Why is a dot model useful for studying matter?
A) The dots are the real size of particles
B) It helps us picture particles too small to see
C) It proves matter has no particles
D) It makes matter disappear
items.answer: B) It helps us picture particles too small to see

steps: Models represent things we cannot directly observe.

items.prompt:
A gas is moved into a much larger sealed container. What happens?
A) It stays in one corner
B) It spreads out to fill the container
C) It turns into a solid
D) It disappears
items.answer: B) It spreads out to fill the container

steps: Gas particles move apart to fill all available space.

items.prompt:
Sugar is stirred into water and the water level barely changes. The best explanation is that
A) the sugar was destroyed
B) sugar particles fit into spaces between water particles
C) water has no particles
D) the sugar became water
items.answer: B) sugar particles fit into spaces between water particles

steps: Small sugar particles settle into the gaps between water particles, so volume changes little.

items.prompt:
A capped syringe of air is pushed so the air takes up less space, with no air escaping. The number of air particles inside
A) increased
B) decreased
C) stayed the same but moved closer together
D) turned into liquid
items.answer: C) stayed the same but moved closer together

steps: No particles left, so the same particles are simply squeezed into less space.
